entry.title: Theranos died in 2018. Who JUST renewed its Patents... and WHY?

media:group.media:title: Theranos died in 2018. Who JUST renewed its Patents... and WHY?
media:group.media:description:
Previously on As the Lab Turns: Theranos died in 2018. Its patent never got the memo.
IN THIS EPISODE: a 19-year-old with a health monitor you swallow. A bird flu plan nobody ran past the chickens. And a "Health Shield" with a familiar-sounding quarantine written 10 years BEFORE Covid.
Then, years after the funeral, somebody pays Theranos' patent bills.
Who? And why?
THE PRINTED ISSUE SIDE EYE: The Loser's Issue (Issue 1) is in print. Includes pages. None require a finger prick. Get it on Amazon: https://a.co/d/02FwgFhM (or search "side eye magazine")
CHAPTERS 0:00 The Patent Has a Pulse 0:18 Nineteen, Swallowable, Now With Chickens 1:12 Pawn Shop, Patent Edition 1:42 Set It and Forget It
ONE QUESTION FOR THE COMMENTS What should the unsigned card on Health Shield's renewal payment say? Rule: write it as a soap opera secret admirer. No names, because the record doesn't have one.
THE FILES WE KEPT - US 8,862,448 (Health Shield), granted Oct 2014, plus its paid-up sisters 9,460,263; 11,139,084; 11,158,429; 11,195,624 - USPTO assignment records: Theranos IP Company, pledged to Fortress Credit Corp. (Dec 2017), renamed Labrador Diagnostics (March 2020) - USPTO maintenance-fee record: Health Shield's 12th-year fee, paid April 1, 2026 - Labrador Diagnostics LLC v. BioFire Diagnostics (D. Del. 1:20-cv-00348), asserting US 8,283,155 and 10,533,994 - Labrador's March 16, 2020 press release: "an entity owned by investment funds managed by Fortress"
FULL SOURCE FILE: https://tinyurl.com/sideeye-theranos-v1-sources

media:group.media:title: Napoleon Was Their Third Pick
media:group.media:description:
Whose man was Napoleon? And who was their first choice?
Somebody went shopping for a general to front a takeover. On the morning of the coup, France’s government bonds jumped, before anyone knew it would work.
Heather thinks somebody knew. Edwin would like a list of who was buying. History, allegedly.
THE PRINTED ISSUE SIDE EYE: The Loser's Issue. Our Napoleon feature, "Not a Loser. Not Short. Not Alone.", lays out the job posting, the crew, the bond market and the bank, with what we can prove and what we can't, side by side. Bonus: DRESS THE HIRE, a cut-out Napoleon paper doll with HAT NO. 3 (Hats No. 1 and 2 were unavailable). Scissors not included.
Get it on Amazon: https://a.co/d/02FwgFhM Or search "side eye magazine"
CHAPTERS 0:00 The lone genius had a hiring manager 0:44 This is SIDE EYE. History, allegedly. 1:03 Egypt: 1 star, would not invade again 1:29 167,000 francs: not even three hours of France 2:35 Wanted: one hero. Must bring own army. 2:50 The lone genius had a group chat 3:14 Bonds jump early. Total coincidence. 3:35 Day two goes about as well as Egypt 4:04 20 assassins reported, 1 brother confirmed 4:36 Did the bankers buy the coup? Asking. 4:56 Napoleon buys 30 shares. A modest position. 5:56 A free press (13 papers remaining) 6:33 Total enemies, joint bank account 6:46 Haiti's revolution and the Louisiana sale 7:51 Treason, but make it go through Amsterdam 8:17 25 million pesos take the scenic route 8:35 Great week at work, bank run at home 9:21 Owe the state 141 million? Sit very still. 10:13 His Senate objects, just 14 years late 10:56 Laffitte updates his LinkedIn, same day 11:16 Exit interview: millions to the bookkeeper 11:50 Third choice, promoted to temp 11:56 The tax money, living rent free at the bank 12:56 Ouvrard, the guy who catered both teams 13:27 Next: Ross Perot tries to Venmo for hostages
ONE QUESTION FOR THE COMMENTS Who actually won: the general, the bankers or the bookkeeper? You're not allowed to answer "France."

entry.title: How Rupert Murdoch's dad + Emu Wars changed today's media

media:group.media:title: How Rupert Murdoch's dad + Emu Wars changed today's media
media:group.media:description:
EMUS 1, ARMY 0. That's the meme. The reality: the farmers got the bill. The family behind Fox News got the playbook.
The army brought machine guns. Keith Murdoch's papers brought the jokes. His son Rupert later built The Sun, The Wall Street Journal and Fox News.
Heather believes the version everybody learned. Edwin brought the receipts. History, allegedly.
THE PRINTED ISSUE SIDE EYE: The Loser's Issue. Cover story: "The Emus Didn't Win. The Newspapers Did." Everything we can prove and everything we can't, side by side. Includes EMU COMMANDO, with real newspaper action! Victory not included. Bullets billed separately.
Get it on Amazon: https://a.co/d/02FwgFhM Or search "side eye magazine"
